mainTopic: Combining ראש חודש with another day in one ברכה; saying זמן on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים; and fasting on ערב שבת.
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא asked why, according to בית שמאי, ראש חודש gets no separate ברכה on ראש השנה. רבי זירא answers that ראש חודש is always folded into other ברכות. A ברייתא in which בית שמאי give ראש חודש on שבת its own ברכה challenges him, and the גמרא admits it is a difficulty (קשיא). The גמרא then shows that combining two days in one ברכה is itself a dispute among תנאים. The first opinion combines only in מוסף, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל combines in every seven-ברכה תפילה. רב חסדא and רבה conclude that one mention of זכרון counts for both days. Next, רבה asks whether זמן (שהחיינו) is said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. After a ברייתא, a debate over needing a כוס, and the story of רב חסדא saying זמן at קידוש, the גמרא rules that זמן is said on both days and may be said even without a כוס. Finally, רבה asks whether a student fasting on ערב שבת must finish his fast, and רבא begins a proof from a ברייתא about תשעה באב on שבת that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ראש חודש is different because it is always folded in
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains why, even for בית שמאי, ראש חודש does not get its own ברכה in מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: ראש חודש is different. Since it is included inside the regular ברכות of שחרית and ערבית, it is also included inside the ברכה of מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the earlier question. He explains why ראש חודש does not need a separate ברכה in מוסף, even according to בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש חודש never has its own ברכה in שחרית or ערבית. We just mention it inside another ברכה. רבי זירא argues that the same pattern should carry over to מוסף, so ראש חודש is 'כולל', folded into the other day's ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because of the fact that
Includes / combines (mentioning a day inside another ברכה instead of giving it its own)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Rosh Chodesh is different,
since one includes it in the morning and evening prayers,
phrases.notes: There is no separate ברכה for ראש חודש in these prayers. It is mentioned inside another ברכה.

phrases.english: one also includes it in the additional prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: שָׁאנֵי רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier: why ראש חודש has no separate ברכה on ראש השנה according to בית שמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): ראש חודש is a special category that is always combined.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בית שמאי give every day its own ברכה, ראש חודש should also need its own ברכה in מוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: ראש חודש is always included inside other ברכות, so it is included in מוסף as well.

steps.title: Challenge: בית שמאי require eight ברכות when ראש חודש falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with a ברייתא in which בית שמאי give ראש חודש its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do בית שמאי really accept 'combining'? But a ברייתא taught: When ראש חודש falls on שבת, בית שמאי say one davens eight ברכות, and בית הלל say one davens seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's answer. It brings a ברייתא showing that בית שמאי do NOT combine ראש חודש with שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal שבת מוסף has seven ברכות. Eight ברכות means ראש חודש gets its own separate ברכה. So בית שמאי seem to reject 'כולל' even for ראש חודש, which goes directly against רבי זירא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Eight' and 'seven' here count the ברכות of the שבת מוסף, not of a weekday שמונה עשרה. Seven is the normal שבת number. Eight means an extra, separate ברכה for ראש חודש.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לְהוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי כּוֹלֵל?
phrases.english: But do Beit Shammai hold of 'including'?
But it was taught in a baraita:
Rosh Chodesh that falls on Shabbat,
Beit Shammai say: one prays eight blessings,
phrases.notes: This means a separate ברכה for ראש חודש.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: one prays seven.
phrases.notes: שבת and ראש חודש share one ברכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לְהוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי כּוֹלֵל? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's answer from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that בית שמאי combine ראש חודש into another ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows בית שמאי require eight ברכות when ראש חודש falls on שבת, which means a separate ברכה. That contradicts the idea that they 'combine'.

steps.title: The challenge stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the ברייתא poses a real difficulty for רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the exchange by saying 'קשיא': the question remains and no answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' is weaker than 'תיובתא' (a full refutation). The problem is left open without fully rejecting the view. Here it means רבי זירא's answer runs into an unresolved problem from the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stands unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא said בית שמאי fold ראש חודש into other ברכות. A ברייתא shows בית שמאי giving ראש חודש on שבת its own ברכה (eight). The גמרא leaves this as an open difficulty.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Step 2 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's explanation is left facing an unresolved difficulty from the ברייתא of eight ברכות.

steps.title: Combining days is itself a dispute; the weekday-style prayers on such a שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that 'combining' is debated among תנאים. It cites a ברייתא: on a שבת that is also ראש חודש or חול המועד, ערבית, שחרית and מנחה stay at seven ברכות, with a mention of the day in the ברכה of עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The idea of 'combining' itself is a dispute among תנאים. As a ברייתא taught: When שבת falls on ראש חודש or חול המועד, one davens ערבית, שחרית and מנחה in the normal way, seven ברכות. He mentions the special day in the ברכה of עבודה (רצה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new observation: whether we combine days in one ברכה is debated among תנאים. It starts quoting a ברייתא to show this, and this first part sets up the rest of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this first opinion, in ערבית, שחרית and מנחה the extra day does not get its own ברכה. The davening stays at seven, and the day is mentioned (יעלה ויבא) inside רצה, not combined into the שבת ברכה. The dispute over 'combining' appears when רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל (step 7) combine the day into the שבת ברכה in these תפילות too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
The intermediate days of a festival (חול המועד)

steps.confusionAlert: Mentioning the day inside רצה (יעלה ויבא) is not the same as 'combining' two days into one ברכה of קדושת היום. The first opinion combines only in מוסף (step 6), while the next opinion (step 7) combines in every seven-ברכה תפילה.

phrases.english: And 'including' itself is a dispute of the tanna'im,
as it was taught in a baraita:
Shabbat that falls on Rosh Chodesh
or on the intermediate days of a Festival,
for the evening, morning, and afternoon prayers
one prays in his usual way, seven blessings,
and says a passage matching the occasion in the Temple-service blessing.
phrases.notes: This refers to יעלה ויבא in רצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After leaving the קשיא open, the גמרא points out that the concept of 'combining' is itself debated among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a שבת that is also ראש חודש or חול המועד, ערבית, שחרית and מנחה are seven ברכות, with the day mentioned in עבודה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: mention the day in הודאה; forgetting requires repeating
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר places the mention of the day in the ברכה of הודאה instead of עבודה. Someone who leaves it out must go back and daven again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the mention goes in the ברכה of הודאה (מודים). And if he did not say it, we make him go back.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי אליעזר disagrees about where to insert the mention of the special day. Then the ברייתא states that leaving it out requires repeating the תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions argue only about placement: עבודה (רצה) versus הודאה (מודים). Both agree the day must be mentioned. The rule that one must go back shows the mention is required, not optional.

keyTerms.meaning: We make him go back and repeat

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: in the thanksgiving blessing,
and if he did not say it, we make him go back.
phrases.notes: This may belong to רבי אליעזר's statement, or it can be read as a general rule of the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a dissenting opinion about where the mention goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the mention of the day goes in הודאה, and omitting it requires repeating the תפילה.

steps.title: In מוסף, שבת and the special day share one ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that in מוסף, the middle ברכה opens and closes with שבת, and the holiness of the special day is mentioned in the middle. This is a clear case of 'combining'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in מוסף, he begins with the שבת section and ends with the שבת section, and he mentions the holiness of the day (ראש חודש or the festival) in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The first תנא of the ברייתא now gives his rule for מוסף: here the two days are combined into one ברכה. This sets up the dispute in the next step, where other תנאים apply the same combining to every תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first תנא, מוסף is different from the other תפילות. ראש חודש or the festival does not get a separate ברכה. Instead it is placed inside the שבת ברכה, which opens and closes with שבת. In ערבית, שחרית and מנחה he only mentions the day in עבודה (step 4), and that is where the next opinion disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the day (the special day's middle section)

steps.whatToRemember: In ערבית, שחרית and מנחה, the special day is only mentioned inside רצה (or מודים according to רבי אליעזר). In מוסף, the special day is combined into the שבת ברכה: it starts with שבת, ends with שבת, and the special day goes in the middle. This is the classic model of 'כולל'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for how we daven מוסף on שבת ראש חודש and שבת חול המועד: one combined middle ברכה that ends with שבת.

phrases.english: And in the additional prayer, one begins with that of Shabbat,
and concludes with that of Shabbat,
and says the sanctity of the day in the middle.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues next with further opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of the ברייתא for מוסף. This is where the 'combining' model actually appears.

steps.title: The second opinion: combining in every seven-ברכה תפילה
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה rule that in every תפילה of seven ברכות, the middle ברכה opens and closes with שבת and mentions the special day in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה say: in every תפילה that has seven ברכות, you begin the middle ברכה with שבת, end it with שבת, and mention the holiness of the special day in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the תנאים debate. These תנאים apply the 'combining' method to ערבית, שחרית and מנחה too, not only to מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, the first opinion placed the mention of the special day in עבודה during the regular תפילות. These תנאים say that every seven-ברכה תפילה works like מוסף: the special day goes inside the שבת ברכה. This makes 'combining' the standard method all day long.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires seven ברכות (a שבת or יום טוב tefillah)
Begins and concludes (the opening and closing of the ברכה)
The holiness of the day (the middle ברכה about the special day)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'combining' two days into one ברכה is a real and widespread method among the תנאים. That gives support to the idea that one mention can cover two occasions.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, say:
Wherever one is required to say seven blessings,
phrases.notes: This includes ערבית, שחרית and מנחה, not just מוסף.

phrases.english: he begins with Shabbat
and concludes with Shabbat,
and he says the holiness of the day in the middle.
phrases.notes: This refers to ראש חודש or יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the second side of the ברייתא's debate and widens 'combining' from מוסף to all seven-ברכה תפילות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every seven-ברכה תפילה, the special day is mentioned inside the שבת ברכה, which opens and closes with שבת.

steps.title: What was decided in the end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion was on the original question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the conclusion about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the original question about mentioning two special days together, such as ראש השנה that falls on ראש חודש. It asks for the final ruling and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the challenge to רבי זירא and the survey of the תנאים, the issue has not yet been settled. This short question asks for the bottom line, which step 9 gives.

keyTerms.meaning: What became of it? (What was the final conclusion?)

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תנאים survey and returns to the main open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final halachic ruling on whether one mention can cover both days.

steps.title: One mention of זכרון counts for both
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה both rule that one mention of זכרון counts for both occasions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: one mention of remembrance counts for this and for that. And רבה said the same: one mention of remembrance counts for this and for that.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give the same answer. One mention of זכרון covers both special days, so a separate mention is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the question in favor of 'combining'. A single זכרון mention covers both days, which fits the תנאים who allow two days to share one ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Remembrance (the theme of ראש השנה; ראש חודש is also called a day of זכרון)
For this and for that (for both days)

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows 'combining': one mention of זכרון covers both days.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: זִכָּרוֹן אֶחָד עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן.
phrases.english: One mention of remembrance counts for both this and that.
And so too Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: זִכָּרוֹן אֶחָד עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן.
phrases.english: One mention of remembrance counts for both this and that.
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the line to show that two separate אמוראים agree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא זִכָּרוֹן אֶחָד עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One mention of זכרון counts for both days; no separate mention is required.

steps.title: Must one say זמן on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: רבה recalls a question raised in רב הונא's בית מדרש: is זמן (שהחיינו) said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים? רב הונא had no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: when I was in רב הונא's בית מדרש, we asked: should one say זמן on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים? Maybe yes, because these days come from one season to the next. Or maybe no, because they are not called רגלים. רב הונא did not have an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new but related topic about ראש השנה. רבה asks whether זמן is said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. רב הונא had no answer; the discussion continues, and the final ruling comes in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason to say it: these days return at fixed times each year, which is what זמן celebrates. The reason not to say it: they are not counted among the רגלים, the joyous festivals where זמן is said. רב הונא could not decide, so the question continues in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We had a question (an open dilemma)
It comes from one season to the next (returns at fixed times)
The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
He did not have it in hand (he had no answer)

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
When I was in the house of study of Rav Huna,
we raised a dilemma:
What is the law about saying the blessing of 'time'
on Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur?
Since they come from season to season, do we say it?
phrases.notes: This is the side that says yes.

phrases.english: Or perhaps
since they are not called pilgrimage festivals,
we do not say it?
phrases.notes: This is the side that says no.

phrases.english: He (Rav Huna) did not have an answer at hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוֵינָא בֵּי רַב הוּנָא אִיבַּעְיָא לַן מַהוּ לוֹמַר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about the special days of ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שהחיינו is said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, since they return yearly but are not רגלים.

steps.title: רב יהודה: I say זמן even on a new gourd
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that he says זמן even on a new gourd, so he would surely say it on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came to רב יהודה's בית מדרש, he said: I say זמן even on a new gourd.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings his question to רב יהודה. רב יהודה answers that he says זמן even over something as small as a new gourd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If זמן can be said over a new gourd, then it can certainly be said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. But this only shows that saying it is allowed. It does not show that it is required, and the next step makes exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: A new gourd (a new seasonal fruit or vegetable)

phrases.english: When I came to the house of study of Rav Yehuda,
he said:
I, over a new gourd,
also say the blessing of 'time'.
phrases.notes: So he would surely say it on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי בֵּי רַב יְהוּדָה אֲמַר אֲנָא אַקָּרָא חַדְתָּא נָמֵי אָמֵינָא זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A first attempt to answer the dilemma in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זמן may be said even over a new gourd, so it may certainly be said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: The real question: optional or required?
steps.stepSummary: רבה clarifies that he never doubted that one may say זמן. He wants to know whether one must say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: I was not asking whether it is allowed. What I am asking is whether it is required. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה points out that רב יהודה's answer misses the point. He sharpens his question: is זמן on these days required, or only allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between רשות (you may) and חובה (you must). The new gourd proves only רשות. רבה wants to know about חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a question for me (what I am asking)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not disagreeing with רב יהודה. He agrees that one may say זמן. He is only explaining that his question was about obligation.

phrases.english: I said to him:
About the option, I have no question;
what I am asking about
is obligation: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: רְשׁוּת לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי חוֹבָה מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 11 answered only whether זמן is allowed, and narrows the question to whether it is required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is an obligation to say זמן on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: זמן is required only on the three רגלים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב and שמואל: one is required to say זמן only on the three רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: רב and שמואל both said that one says זמן only on the three רגלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the sharpened question by quoting רב and שמואל. The obligation to say זמן applies only on the three רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports the 'no' side of רבה's original dilemma. Since ראש השנה and יום הכפורים are not רגלים, there is no obligation to say זמן on them, although saying it is still allowed (step 11).
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב and שמואל, זמן is required only on the three רגלים. On ראש השנה and יום הכפורים it is רשות, not חובה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final word. The גמרא continues the discussion, and in practice we do say שהחיינו on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: He said to me:
It was Rav and Shmuel who both said:
One does not say the blessing of 'time'
except on the three pilgrimage festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ אֵין אוֹמֵר זְמַן אֶלָּא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sharpened question about obligation from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Saying זמן is required only on the three רגלים, so it is not required on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought to challenge רב ושמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא on the פסוק 'תן חלק לשבעה וגם לשמונה'. According to רבי יהושע, the word 'וגם' includes עצרת, ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'Give a portion to seven and also to eight.' רבי אליעזר says: 'Seven' means the seven days of creation, and 'eight' means the eight days until מילה. רבי יהושע says: 'Seven' means the seven days of פסח, and 'eight' means the eight days of סוכות. And when it says 'and also', it comes to include שבועות, ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב ושמואל from the previous step. This step only sets up the source. The actual point of the attack comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע reads the פסוק as being about the holidays. The word 'וגם' adds ראש השנה and יום הכפורים to the list. That seems to put them in the same category as the רגלים, which conflicts with רב ושמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Give a portion to seven and also to eight' (קהלת יא:ב)
The eight days until a baby's ברית מילה
To include (the word 'גם' adds something extra)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get stuck on רבי אליעזר's reading. Only רבי יהושע's reading about the holidays matters for the challenge.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"Give a portion to seven, and also to eight"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from קהלת יא:ב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"Seven" — these are the seven days of Creation;
"Eight" — these are the eight days until circumcision.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
"Seven" — these are the seven days of Passover;
"Eight" — these are the eight days of the Festival (Sukkot).
And when it says "and also" —

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת עֲצֶרֶת וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: it comes to include Shavuot, Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא against רב ושמואל's ruling in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל: זמן is required only on the three רגלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא groups ראש השנה and יום הכפורים with the רגלים, which suggests the same requirement applies to them.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to be about זמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the 'portion' in the ברייתא is the ברכה of זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about זמן?
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא states the point of the challenge. The ברייתא seems to require זמן on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, against רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'portion' is זמן, then זמן is required on all the days listed. That would include ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, which directly contradicts 'only on the three רגלים'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading used as an attack)

phrases.english: What, is it not referring to the blessing of time (She'hecheyanu)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא contradicts רב ושמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading 'portion' as זמן makes זמן required on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: The ברייתא means the ברכה of the day, not זמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'portion' is the special ברכה of the day's holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the ברכה of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ושמואל. It says the ברייתא is not about זמן at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'portion' is the ברכה that mentions the day's קדושה, like in קידוש or תפילה. Every holiday on the list has that ברכה, including ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. So the ברייתא says nothing about זמן, and רב ושמואל stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the ברכה of the day's קדושה (קדושת היום)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is about the ברכה of the day's holiness, not about שהחיינו. So רב ושמואל's 'only on the three רגלים' still stands.

phrases.english: No, it refers to the blessing (of the day's sanctity).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'portion' is the ברכה of the day's קדושה

steps.title: A proof that the ברייתא is not about זמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the answer makes sense. זמן is not said on all seven days of פסח, yet the ברייתא counts all seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you thought it meant זמן, is זמן said on all seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks of 'seven days of פסח', as if each day gets the 'portion'. זמן is normally said only once, at the start of the holiday. So the 'portion' must be the ברכה of the day, which is said every day.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces supporting reasoning)
If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if it would enter your mind that it refers to the blessing of time —
is there a blessing of time all seven days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 16
steps.raayaObject: The 'portion' in the ברייתא is the ברכה of the day, not זמן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא counts all seven days, but זמן is said only once

steps.title: זמן can be made up on any day of the holiday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. All seven days are 'days of זמן' because if one did not say it today, he can say it on a later day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. If he did not say the ברכה today, he says it tomorrow or on another day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זמן is said only once, but that once can happen on any day of the holiday. So the ברייתא could count all seven days even if it means זמן. The proof falls away, though the answer itself is still possible.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult (introduces a rejection)

steps.confusionAlert: Only the proof is rejected here. The answer from step 16 ('it refers to the ברכה') is not cancelled.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
for if he does not recite the blessing today —
he recites it tomorrow or on another day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the supporting proof, not the תירוץ of step 16
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed זמן belongs only to the first day. In fact it can be made up on any day of the holiday.

steps.title: Does this support רב נחמן that זמן needs no כוס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the case of making up זמן on a later day. A כוס of wine is needed, yet there is usually no כוס then. Perhaps this supports רב נחמן, who says זמן may be said even in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, don't we need a כוס? Let us say this supports רב נחמן, for רב נחמן said: one may say זמן even in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on the idea that זמן can be said on a later day. It suggests this proves רב נחמן's view that no כוס is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally זמן is said over the כוס of קידוש. On the middle days there is no קידוש and usually no כוס. If one can still say זמן then, it must work without a כוס, just as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of wine over which a ברכה is said
Let us say it supports him
In the market (anywhere, without a כוס)

phrases.english: In any case — do we not require a cup?
Let us say this supports Rav Naḥman.
For Rav Naḥman said:
The blessing of time — one may say it even in the market.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new inference from the rejection in step 18
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן: זמן may be said without a כוס, even in the market
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that זמן can be made up on later days of the holiday, when there is usually no כוס

steps.title: The case is when he happened to have a כוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב נחמן. Making up זמן on a later day refers to someone who happens to have a כוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. It is when a כוס happened to come his way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this side-discussion. It rejects the support for רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The make-up rule can apply to someone who has a כוס of wine on a later day. So it does not prove that זמן works without a כוס. רב נחמן's view is not proven from here.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened to come his way

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove that זמן works without a כוס. Making up זמן on later days refers to someone who happens to have a כוס.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
for it is a case where a cup happened to come his way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, דְּאִיקְּלַע לֵיהּ כּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support for רב נחמן proposed in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof for רב נחמן, without deciding the halacha against him
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed there is no כוס on later days. The case can be one where he happened to have a כוס.

steps.title: How can one say זמן over a cup on יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: Saying זמן over a כוס works on שבועות and ראש השנה. But on יום הכפורים, if he drinks the wine after saying זמן, he has already accepted the fast, so the wine is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for שבועות and ראש השנה, but what does one do on יום הכפורים? If he blesses over the cup and drinks it, then once he said זמן he accepted the day upon himself, and the wine is forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a practical problem: on יום הכפורים there seems to be no workable way to say זמן over a כוס of wine. It knocks out the first option, which is to bless and drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said זמן needs a כוס. On a regular יום טוב that is easy, because it is said during קידוש. On יום הכפורים, saying זמן means he is accepting the holiness of the day, and with it the fast. So drinking the wine right after the ברכה is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (granted for this case, but what about the other case?)
How does he act / what does he do?
He accepted it (the holiness of the day) upon himself
And it became forbidden to him

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that wine is forbidden before יום הכפורים begins. The problem is that saying זמן is itself an acceptance of the day, so from that moment he is fasting.

phrases.english: This works well for Shavuos and Rosh HaShana,
phrases.notes: On those days there is קידוש over wine, so זמן can be said over that כוס.

phrases.english: but on Yom Kippur, what does one do?
If he blesses over it and drinks it,
phrases.notes: This would be done before the fast, on ערב יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: since he said זמן,
he accepted the day upon himself, and the wine is forbidden to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח עֲצֶרֶת וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הֵיכִי עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 20's assumption that זמן needs a כוס, and challenges how that can work on יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of saying זמן over a כוס, as it applies to יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying זמן accepts the day. Once the fast has been accepted, the wine cannot be drunk.

steps.title: Proof that saying the blessing means accepting the day
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא saw רב make קידוש early and asked if he had now stopped doing מלאכה. רב said yes. This shows that reciting the day's ברכה brings the day's rules into effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב ירמיה בר אבא said to רב: Have you now separated from work? And he said to him: Yes, I have separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the claim from step 21. Saying the day's ברכה really does count as accepting the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב made קידוש before שבת actually began. He confirmed that from that point on he was keeping שבת. By the same logic, saying זמן before יום הכפורים makes the fast start for him immediately.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב:
phrases.english: For Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said to Rav:
phrases.notes: He had seen רב make קידוש before שבת actually started.

phrases.english: Have you separated (from work)?
And he said to him: Yes, I have separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 21 that saying זמן counts as accepting the day.
steps.raayaObject: Reciting the day's ברכה (קידוש or זמן) means accepting the day's holiness and its rules
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's answer to רב ירמיה בר אבא, confirming that he stopped doing מלאכה after an early קידוש

steps.title: He cannot bless and leave the cup untouched
steps.stepSummary: A second option is to say זמן over the כוס and set it aside without drinking. This fails, because one who makes a ברכה over a כוס must taste from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him bless over it and set it aside. But one who blesses must taste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a second way out and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the wine undrunk avoids breaking the fast. However, there is a rule that whoever makes a ברכה over a כוס must taste from it. Without that, the ברכה over the כוס is pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him set it down (leave it)
One who makes a ברכה must taste

phrases.english: Let him bless over it and set it aside —
one who blesses must taste!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a second solution to the problem in step 21 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion to bless over the כוס without drinking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that one who blesses over a כוס must taste from it makes this impossible.

steps.title: He cannot give the cup to a child
steps.stepSummary: A third option is to give the wine to a child, who is not fasting. This is rejected because the הלכה does not follow רב אחא on this. The child might get used to drinking wine on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him give it to a child. But the halacha is not like רב אחא, because perhaps the child will come to be drawn after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one last solution and rejects it too. Every option for saying זמן over a כוס on יום הכפורים has now failed. The final ruling in step 28 (זמן needs no כוס) resolves this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child is not obligated to fast, so he could drink the wine. But we are concerned that the child will become used to it and keep drinking on יום הכפורים even after he grows up. Therefore we do not follow רב אחא, who allowed giving such a כוס to a child.

keyTerms.meaning: To be drawn after it (to get used to it)

steps.whatToRemember: All three ways of saying זמן over a כוס on יום הכפורים fail: drinking it, leaving it, and giving it to a child. This sets up the practical question of what the ruling actually is.

phrases.english: Let him give it to a child —
the halacha is not like Rav Acha,
phrases.notes: רב אחא elsewhere allowed giving such a כוס to a child.

phrases.english: because perhaps he will come to be drawn after it.
phrases.notes: He might keep drinking on יום הכפורים even after he grows up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a third solution after step 23 and rejects it, closing off every option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion to give the כוס to a child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה does not follow רב אחא, because of the concern that the child will get used to drinking on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: What is the ruling? The Sages send someone to watch רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final ruling is. The רבנן sent רב יימר סבא to watch how רב חסדא acted on ערב ראש השנה and report back.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about it? The רבנן sent רב יימר סבא to רב חסדא on ערב ראש השנה. They told him: Go see how he acts in practice, and come tell us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical ruling. It is setting up the answer, which will come from watching what רב חסדא actually does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the reasoning did not settle the matter, the רבנן decided to learn from a great רבי's actual practice. רב יימר סבא was sent to observe whether רב חסדא says זמן on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?
The Rabbis sent Rav Yeimar the Elder
before Rav Chisda
on the eve of Rosh HaShana.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: זִיל חֲזִי הֵיכִי עָבֵיד עוֹבָדָא,
phrases.english: They said to him: Go see how he acts in practice,
and come tell us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After every option fails in steps 21-24, the גמרא asks for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether זמן is actually said on ראש השנה (and יום הכפורים), as shown by a great רבי's practice

steps.title: רב חסדא makes קידוש and says זמן
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא realized that רב יימר had come for a reason, and said so with a folk saying. They brought him a כוס of wine, and he made קידוש and said זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב חסדא saw him, he said: One who lifts up a moist log wants it for something right here. They brought him a cup of wine, and he made קידוש and said זמן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר watches רב חסדא and sees him say זמן during קידוש on ראש השנה. This answers the practical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wet log is useless as firewood, so someone who picks it up must want it for a specific purpose. רב חסדא was hinting that רב יימר clearly had a purpose in visiting. His action shows that זמן is said on ראש השנה, over the כוס of קידוש.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, רב חסדא said זמן on ראש השנה during קידוש over a כוס of wine.
steps.confusionAlert: The saying about the wet log is not part of the הלכה. It is only רב חסדא's way of telling רב יימר that he knew why he had come.

phrases.english: When he saw him, he said to him:
One who lifts up a moist log
wants it for something right here.
phrases.notes: A folk saying meaning "you surely came here with a purpose."

phrases.english: They brought him a cup of wine,
he made kiddush and said זמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 by reporting רב חסדא's actual practice.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא said זמן on ראש השנה over the כוס of קידוש, showing that זמן is said on ראש השנה
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, in practice, זמן is said on ראש השנה. It also shows the common Talmudic method of settling a question by watching how a great רבי actually behaves.

steps.title: Final ruling: זמן is said on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the ברכה of זמן is said on both ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: one says זמן on ראש השנה and on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: After the long discussion and the story of רב חסדא, the גמרא gives the final ruling: זמן is said on ראש השנה and on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier רבה asked whether there is an obligation to say זמן on these days, since they are not called רגלים, and רב ושמואל said it is required only on the three רגלים. The story of רב חסדא saying זמן with קידוש on ראש השנה settles it in practice: זמן is said on both days.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of שהחיינו, said on a new season or festival

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for saying שהחיינו on ראש השנה and on יום הכפורים in practice.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: one says the blessing of 'time'
on Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: This rests on the story of רב חסדא in step 26.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: אוֹמֵר זְמַן בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב חסדא's practice into the official ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: זמן is said on both ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: זמן may be said anywhere, even in the market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that זמן does not need a כוס of wine and may be said even in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: זמן may be said even in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second ruling: you do not need a כוס of wine to say זמן. You can say it anywhere, even in the market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This solves the יום הכפורים problem from steps 23 and 24. There, no one could drink the wine. If זמן does not need a כוס at all, one can just say it without wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Market, a public place with no כוס of wine

steps.whatToRemember: Two rulings close the זמן discussion. First, זמן is said on ראש השנה and on יום הכפורים. Second, זמן does not need a כוס, so on יום הכפורים it is simply said without wine.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: the blessing of 'time' —
one may say it even in the market.
phrases.notes: In other words, no כוס of wine is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling that removes the practical problem of the כוס on יום הכפורים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: זמן does not need a כוס, so it can be said anywhere.

steps.title: Must a student fasting on ערב שבת finish his fast?
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports a question from רב הונא's study hall: must a student fasting on ערב שבת complete the fast until nightfall? Neither רב הונא nor רב יהודה knew the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה also said: When we were in רב הונא's study hall, we asked: a student who is fasting on ערב שבת, must he complete his fast? רב הונא did not know. I went to רב יהודה, and he did not know either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבה tells of another question from his student days: if a student is fasting on ערב שבת, does he keep fasting into שבת, or does he stop before?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is a conflict between two values. Finishing a fast you took on is good. But entering שבת hungry and weak hurts the honor and enjoyment of שבת. Two great teachers had no tradition on this, so in the next step רבא looks for an answer in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: We asked (a real question we did not know the answer to)
A student in the study hall
He did not have it in hand; he had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: בַּר בֵּי רַב does not mean 'the son of רב.' It is a common phrase for a student in the study hall.

phrases.english: And Rabba said,
when we were in the house of study of Rav Huna,
we raised a question:
a student who is sitting in a fast
on Shabbat eve,
what is the law about completing it?
phrases.notes: Does he fast until night, or stop before שבת so he does not enter it weak?

phrases.english: He (Rav Huna) did not have an answer at hand.
I came before Rav Yehuda,
and he did not have an answer at hand either.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה, כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב הוּנָא אִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question linked to the earlier one by the same source: both come from רבה's student days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person fasting on ערב שבת must keep fasting until nightfall, into שבת, or must stop before שבת.

steps.title: רבא begins a proof from a ברייתא about תשעה באב on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests finding the answer in the sources himself, and begins quoting a ברייתא about תשעה באב that falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Let us look into it ourselves, for it was taught in a ברייתא: 'תשעה באב that falls on שבת...'
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבא says the answer can be found in a ברייתא and starts quoting it. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the teachers had no tradition, רבא turns to a written source. A ברייתא about תשעה באב falling on שבת deals with a fast that runs up against שבת, so it may show how such a clash is handled. The actual proof comes once the full ברייתא is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us look into it ourselves
The fast of the Ninth of Av

phrases.english: Rava said: Let us look at it ourselves,
as it was taught in a baraita:
the Ninth of Av that occurs on Shabbat
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the unanswered question of step 29 by looking for a source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one completes a fast on ערב שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about תשעה באב that falls on שבת (quote continues on the next amud).
